findings.where: design.md §3 acceptance gate 'grep -ri DRAWING services/queue returns empty', §8, §7 ADR; vs live services/queue/internal/queue/application/usecase/my_entry.go lines 96 & 101, application/usecase/join.go line 161, infrastructure/valkey/queue_store.go hashToEntry line 448 (plus residual DRAWING comments/test rows)
findings.problem: The design commits to a mechanical gate ('grep -ri DRAWING services/queue' must be empty) but its §3 REMOVE enumeration names only a subset of DRAWING sites. A fresh grep returns live code branches §3 never names: my_entry.go:101 (|| ent.Status == valueobject.StatusDrawing disjunct), my_entry.go:96 (!doc.Drawing zone-emit guard), join.go:161 (ent.Status == valueobject.StatusDrawing special-case suppressing direct admission), and queue_store.go:448 in hashToEntry (else if e.Status != valueobject.StatusDrawing rank-backfill branch). A coder editing exactly what §3 lists leaves these in place; moreover §3 DOES delete valueobject.StatusDrawing, so those three StatusDrawing references stop compiling (undefined symbol) and the §8 `go build ./...` gate breaks on edits §3 never scheduled, while my_entry.go:96 keeps a dead doc.Drawing guard. Either way the §3 'grep empty' gate is unreachable from the §3 list and the task requirement 'position math and the status document have NO leftover DRAWING branches' is not guaranteed. The grep also lists residual DRAWING comments/test rows the enumeration omits (entity/entry.go 14,18; dto/entry_status.go 8,10,13; dto/status_document.go 9; dto/join_request.go 19; anon_values.go 53 + anon_values_test.go 117 on the KEPT NextHeartbeatMs; entry_mapper_test.go 45 enum row; worker/liveness.go 23; port/outbound/types.go 23,46,63; port/outbound/queue_store.go 47), which also keep the gate non-empty and (for entry_mapper_test.go:45) break compilation once the enum is removed.
findings.fix: Make the §3 REMOVE list complete enough that the gate it promises can pass. Add the four live Go branches and route them to plain FIFO: my_entry.go:101 drop the StatusDrawing arm (WAITING/STALE only); my_entry.go:96 drop the !doc.Drawing guard (field is removed); join.go:161 remove the StatusDrawing special-case so JoinCreated always takes the normal audit + tryDirectAdmission path; queue_store.go:448 collapse the 'else if e.Status != StatusDrawing' branch so rank backfills to seq unconditionally. Add the residual DRAWING comments/test rows the grep lists to the cleanup scope (or state they are edited with their owning symbol's removal), including the entry_mapper_test.go:45 enum row and the anon_values NextHeartbeatMs comment+test. Keep the 'grep -ri DRAWING services/queue' gate as the proof the enumeration is complete.

findings.where: design.md §3 ('*Rank -> *Seq revert', 'entity.Entry.Rank removed'); vs join.lua (HSET rank / ZADD waiting rank), heartbeat.lua & liveness.lua (HGET rank), queue_store.go hashToEntry (m['rank'])
findings.problem: §3 reverts the Go-layer *Rank names to *Seq and removes entity.Entry.Rank, but the Lua scripts and the Valkey hash still carry a 'rank' field and score waiting/stale by it. With the draw gone rank==seq always, so FIFO is preserved (not a correctness bug), but the design's intent that 'the *Rank layer carries no information once the draw is gone' is not carried through to the Lua/storage layer, leaving it ambiguous whether the implementer should keep or remove the Lua rank field.
findings.fix: Add one line to §3: either 'the Valkey rank hash field and the ZADD waiting/stale <rank> scores are LEFT AS-IS (already equal seq once the draw is gone); only the Go-facing *Rank symbols are renamed to *Seq', or, for a clean removal, state that join.lua writes seq directly and the rank field is dropped from the hash and hashToEntry.
